An actual convex auxiliary family implies the Minkowski midpoint inclusion at the integer base 1. The required values are all strictly positive, so Brunn–Minkowski in auxiliary dimension r applies to the compact convex sets without lower-dimensional qualifications.

With c the one common positive scale, the endpoint roots are c^(1/r) and c^(1/r)e^(2a/r). Their arithmetic mean is at least c^(1/r)e^(a/r) by AM–GM for every real a, including a=0. The prescribed midpoint root is strictly below this by the factor 2^((1−k)/r)<1.

By product measure, multiplying independent auxiliary fibers into K_z^k yields weight v_z^k|Q_z|. Dividing by the positive v_z^k gives exactly the impossible prescription. This only excludes the independent-volume correction mechanism.
